paper.title: ProgPrompt: Generating Situated Robot Task Plans using Large Language Models
paper.central_claim: Program-like specifications of available actions and objects, executable few-shot examples, comments and assertions enable situated executable plans across environments, capabilities and tasks, improve VirtualHome performance and generalize to a physical robot.

evidence.quote: We present a programmatic LLM prompt structure that enables plan generation functional across situated environments, robot capabilities, and tasks. Our key insight is to prompt the LLM with program-like specifications of the available actions and objects in an environment, as well as with example programs that can be executed. We make concrete recommendations about prompt structure and generation constraints through ablation experiments, demonstrate state of the art success rates in Vir
evidence.support_explanation: Author's broad portability claim and concrete prompting intervention.

evidence.quote: Plan functions consist of API calls to action primitives, comments to summarize actions, and assertions for tracking execution
evidence.support_explanation: Executable plan interface, comments and assertions are distinct operations.

evidence.quote: A VH state \mathbf{s} is a set of objects \mathcal{O} and properties \mathcal{P} . \mathcal{P} encodes information like in ( salmon , microwave ) and agent_close_to ( salmon ). The action space is \mathcal{A}= {grab, putin, putback, walk, find, open, close, switchon, switchoff, sit, standup} . We experiment with 3 VH environments. Each environment contains 115 unique object instances (Fig. 2 ), including class-level duplicates. Each object has properties corresponding to its action affordances. Some objects also have a semantic state
evidence.support_explanation: Simulator supplies symbolic object/property state, a privileged channel unlike physical perception.

evidence.quote: Each result is averaged over 5 runs in a single VH environment across 10 tasks. The variability in performance across runs arises from sampling LLM output. We include 3 Pythonic task plan examples per prompt after evaluating performance on VH for between 1 prompt and 7 prompts and finding that 2 or more prompts result in roughly equal performance for GPT3 . evidence.support_explanation: Repeated simulation denominator and prompt-count selection on VirtualHome; fixed demonstrations disclosed.

evidence.quote:
SR is the fraction of executions that achieved all task-relevant goal-conditions. Exec is the fraction of actions in the plan that are executable in the environment, even if they are not relevant for the task. GCR is measured using the set difference between ground truth final state conditions \mathbf{g} and the final state achieved \mathbf{g}^{\prime} with the generated plan, divided by the number of task-specific goal-conditions; SR =1 only if GCR =1 .

signatures.object: Free-form task-plan representation and robot capability grounding
signatures.information: Instruction, imports of permissible primitive APIs, object list and three fixed example programs; VirtualHome state is symbolic, robot object list comes from ViLD.
signatures.operation: Condition frozen LLM code completion on Pythonic action/object specifications; generate executable primitive-call sequence with natural-language comments.
signatures.output: Plan function calling existing interpreter/robot pick-and-place policy.
signatures.conditions: Permitted APIs and affordances must match actual executor; object perception and action success are not guaranteed.
signatures.feedback: Simulation assertion conditions evaluated using supplied environment state and LLM; no assertion loop in physical setup.
signatures.selection_rule: Static prompt design; number of demonstrations selected on VH; not an autonomous retained-improvement procedure.
signatures.data: 70-task VH pool, fixed three demonstrations; reported main seen-environment evaluation 10 tasks ×5 runs.
signatures.persistence: Static prompt and API library only; no learned cross-task harness update reported.
signatures.later_use: Same prompt structure reused with new object lists and robot API; not a verified growing skill memory.
signatures.claimed_effect: Higher executability, SR and goal-condition recall than text prompting.
signatures.failure_boundary: Unknown affordances, inaccessible objects, perception and gripper failures; strict reference goals can reject alternatives.

signatures.information: Assertions plus simulator object/property state; physical state tracking explicitly insufficient.
signatures.operation: Insert assertions and recovery actions into the generated program, check before proceeding.
signatures.output: A locally repaired action sequence rather than unconstrained free text.
signatures.conditions: Reliable state and truthful precondition check are required; an LLM assertion answer is not an independently calibrated verifier.
signatures.feedback: Per-assertion pass/fail prompts recovery within current task.
signatures.selection_rule: Branch on assertion; no across-task accept/reject optimization.
signatures.data: Same-model feedback/no-feedback comparisons in Table I.
signatures.persistence: Only current execution state; no durable optimized harness.
signatures.failure_boundary: Assertion accuracy itself is not measured; physical demo omits the claimed feedback mechanism.

gap.author_gap: Free-form plans can call nonexistent actions/objects; affordance scoring requires enumerating candidates.
gap.checked_gap: Programmatic action constraints and scene grounding address concrete feasibility failures. They do not solve uncertain physical execution or guarantee correctness of symbolic preconditions.

lineage.method: Huang et al. text-plan generation/semantic matching; SayCan affordance scoring; Inner Monologue feedback; Socratic code completion
lineage.source_version: Descriptions in ProgPrompt 2209.11302v1 II; external original versions not fixed/read
lineage.scope: Paper-local lineage, not an exhaustive prior-art search

gap.closest_adjacent: Inner Monologue already feeds feedback to a planner; code completion already exists. The residual distinction is joint executable action/object prompt schema plus comments and assertions, not the invention of closed-loop planning.
gap.residue: Language plans may be semantically plausible yet non-executable for this robot/current object set.
gap.stakes: Execution halts or fails task goals even when generated text is fluent.
gap.method_response: Explicit imports and objects constrain output; program comments structure subgoals; assertions allow local recovery.
gap.remaining_gap: Symbolic assertions need grounded state; real experiments remove them. Affordance and low-level execution failures remain.
unresolved: Independent attribution to program schema vs extra contextual knowledge is incomplete.
No exhaustive external lineage verification under the no-network fixed-material boundary.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E01 (ablation, common_practice).** Hold the frontier backbone fixed and compare the proposed harness with at least one alternative harness or loop organization on the same episodes. For zero-shot VLN-CE the alternative is a rerun of a published zero-shot harness or workflow (2606.10577#s4, 2609.15195#s4) with the same model; for coding agents, a second deployable harness. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness (rather than the model) raises embodied or agentic success.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a harness (rather than the model) raises embodied or agentic success.
expectations.reason: Same-GPT3 plan-generation comparisons and feedback/comments variants are reported; Codex gains not attributed to harness alone.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E02 (ablation, common_practice).** Attribute a gain to a harness component only through one-at-a-time toggles (leave-one-out or single add) with the backbone fixed. A cumulative stack (A, then +B, then +C) or a bundle-level comparison does not separate components or their interactions. — _applies when_ a claim that a specific harness component (depth tool, memory, verifier, skill library, plugin, feedback channel) causes the improvement.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a specific harness component (depth tool, memory, verifier, skill library, plugin, feedback channel) causes the improvement.
expectations.reason: Comments and feedback toggles exist; verifier reliability and full capability grounding components are not independently audited.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E04 (reproducibility, common_practice).** Report run-to-run variance and use paired task-level statistics: repeated runs per setting, bootstrap or permutation CIs over tasks, and sign tests on discordant episodes. A single run on a 100-episode subset is treated as descriptive. In the read single-run papers, differences of a few points sit within noise. — _applies when_ any success-rate comparison between harnesses, models or training recipes on a fixed task subset.
expectations.applies_when: any success-rate comparison between harnesses, models or training recipes on a fixed task subset.
expectations.reason: Five LLM-sampling runs and dispersions in simulation; robot configurations are single demonstrations and no paired task-level significance test.

expectations.source_strength: common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
source_refs: - **E05 (metric, common_practice).** Report cost alongside success: model calls, input and output tokens, wall-clock or per-call latency, and USD per episode or per solved task, including failed trials. Harnesses with similar pass rates can differ about 40x in tokens per solved task. — _applies when_ a claim that a harness, interface or distilled student is better or more practical than an alternative.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a harness, interface or distilled student is better or more practical than an alternative.
expectations.reason: No complete token/call/latency/financial comparison in all supplied methods/results; primitive and prompt descriptions do not measure cost.
